test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 29 Nov, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that it shall be the duty of every citizen of India to develop scientific temper?
solution:
The correct answer is __**51 A (h)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 51A of the Indian Constitution lists the **Fundamental Duties** of Indian citizens.
 
• Clause (h) of Article 51A specifically mentions that it is the duty of every citizen **to develop scientific temper**, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• This clause was added by the **42nd Amendment Act of 1976**.
 
• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts for their violation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, upon the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Originally, 10 duties were listed, and an 11th duty was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976:**
 
 
• Known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its wide-ranging amendments.
 
• It added the Fundamental Duties and also introduced changes to the Preamble, among other significant changes.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Temper:**
 
 
• Scientific temper refers to an attitude of logical and rational thinking.
 
• It involves questioning, observing physical reality, testing, hypothesizing, analyzing, and communicating.
 
 
 
• **Non-Justiciable Nature:**
 
 
• Fundamental Duties are not enforceable by law, unlike Fundamental Rights.
 
• They serve as moral obligations for the citizens to promote a spirit of patriotism and uphold the unity of India.
